title: Case: Parcel for collection at a corner shop has shown the same status for ten days
context: Order TG-9813, a cast-iron casserole from Pebblewick Goods, was sent as DL-3492 for collection at a pickup point chosen by the recipient at checkout. The recipient account and shipment match are verified.
initial_request: I went into the shop myself this morning. They told me they have been turning parcels away for a fortnight because the back room is full. Mine went BACK. Back to the sender. Nobody told me. Nobody told me it was refused, nobody told me it was sent back, nobody asked me whether I wanted it somewhere else. Ten days of 'on its way to your pickup point' and it was never going to get there. I don't want it at that shop. I am not having it sent to that shop again. Send it to my house, the address is on my account, or tell me who can. Not the shop. I have said this three times to three people now.

events.body: DL-3492 arrived at the destination depot on 25 February for collection at Nettlebank Corner Stores. Tracking has shown 'on its way to your pickup point' since then. We have not checked with the depot why.

Ten days it has said on its way to your pickup point. The shop is four minutes from my front door. Where is it? I asked the chat on your website last week and was told to wait for the collection text.
Please confirm whether DL-3492 has reached you and is ready for collection. The recipient has been waiting since 25 February.
Hi, any update on DL-34965? It was meant to come Monday. Thanks.
Hi, any update on DL-79490? It was meant to come Wednesday. Thanks.

Your message was not delivered. This location has been suspended for parcel intake and messaging since 24 February. Reason given: storage capacity. Messages to a suspended location are not held or forwarded.
DL-3492 has not reached Nettlebank Corner Stores and the location shows as suspended. Please re-attempt handover to the pickup point or advise what is holding it.

Ticket closed, wrong queue. DL-3492 was refused at Nettlebank Corner Stores on 26 February and again on 29 February, reason 'no space'. It was returned to sender on 3 March and is in transit to the Pebblewick warehouse. It is out of our network and we cannot re-attempt it. Our return notice goes to the shipper only, so the recipient will not have been told. Sending a returned order out again, and where to, is for Warehouse dispatch, Pebblewick Goods, through the Warehouse work queue.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Tuesday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

acceptable_actions.summary: Asks Warehouse dispatch to send TG-9813 / DL-3492 out again when it arrives back, to somewhere other than Nettlebank Corner Stores, with the recipient's request for the home address on her account.

must: Asks Warehouse dispatch, through the Warehouse work queue, to re-dispatch TG-9813 / DL-3492 once it is back with them, and passes on the recipient's request that it go to the home address on her account and not to Nettlebank Corner Stores.
Gives the facts from the depot: refused at the shop on 26 February and 29 February for lack of space, returned to sender on 3 March, location suspended for intake since 24 February.
Tells Warehouse dispatch that the recipient was never notified of the refusals or the return and has been waiting since late February, so the re-dispatch can be prioritised.
Leaves the decision and the booking with Warehouse dispatch and does not say that a re-dispatch or a home delivery has been arranged.
must_not: Asks anyone to redeliver the parcel to Nettlebank Corner Stores, or offers the recipient that option.
Sends the request again through the Pickup-point portal or the Depot work queue, or describes the earlier desk messages on those routes as having dealt with it.
Tells the recipient the parcel is on its way to her house, or gives her a delivery date.
Suggests the parcel went back because the recipient failed to collect it.
Replies to the recipient with the tracking status or a request to wait, without acting on the return.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Returned order TG-9813 / DL-3492, recipient Kestra Haverly: please send it out again when it reaches you, and not to the original pickup point. What happened: the parcel was for collection at Nettlebank Corner Stores. The destination depot tells me the shop refused it on 26 February and again on 29 February for lack of space, and it was returned to you on 3 March. The location has been suspended for parcel intake since 24 February. The recipient did nothing wrong. She was never told about the refusals or the return, because the carrier's return notice goes to the shipper only. Tracking showed 'on its way to your pickup point' for ten days and she found out by walking into the shop. She has asked for it to be delivered to the home address on her account and has been clear she does not want that shop again. Please confirm whether you can re-dispatch to the account address and what you need from her to do it. Given the ten days and the lack of any notice, please treat it as a priority. I have not told her anything is booked.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3102: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. 4 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
